xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5100: Telemetry: capture phone and dashboard client errors (failed API reads, crashes, link drops) in PostHog

plan.title: Telemetry: capture phone and dashboard client errors (failed API reads, crashes, link drops) in PostHog
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: One TestFlight build must carry the whole change (the operator uploads phone builds by hand from the Mac rig), and the store privacy declarations must land in the same PR as the first phone analytics or the build ships a false declaration. Of the ~40 files, 17 are tests, docs or store declarations; production code is ~14 small edits across 5 subsystems (contracts, dashboard server, dashboard frontend, phone app, docs). Splitting the phone link-state reporter out would force a second TestFlight build and a second privacy review for the same data categories.

narratives.Problem: Phone and dashboard client errors never reach PostHog. The phone app runs no telemetry at all because the frontend's initTelemetry() reads the admin route GET /api/settings, which a phone token cannot call. On both clients, a failed read such as GET /api/conversations is handled inside the component ("Couldn't load conversations.") and nothing is captured. Link drops and failures on the phone are invisible.
narratives.Proposal: Add two closed-domain events to the telemetry contract: client_request_failed (client, route template, route area, method, status bucket) and phone_link_state (state, reason, route, recovery bucket). Capture request failures with one fetch wrapper (lib/requestFailures.ts) installed outermost on the desktop and, after the channel shims, on the phone; throttle to one event per route/area/status per 60 s. Add GET /api/telemetry/client-config (read:state) so the phone reads the machine's effective telemetry setting, install id, build commit and PostHog key/host; the phone caches the last answer per machine so failures while the link is down are still reported, and a fresh 'off' disables capture. Split the browser door into initTelemetryFromConfig() with client/platform/app_version/build_commit super properties and in-memory persistence plus distinct_id = machine install id on the phone. Add a phone error boundary around MobileApp, a phone link-state reporter driven by dial errors, connection-phase transitions and the route each link used, update the store privacy declarations, and document everything. Full detail: .pan/drafts/PAN-5100.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No QueryCache or MutationCache onError handlers and no query_key_root property (the fetch layer has no query context).
- No telemetry switch in the phone's own Settings and no separate phone telemetry id (PAN-5100 overrides PAN-5021 here).
- No change to the desktop's distinct_id behavior.
- No telemetry on phone shell screens before a machine view opens (sign-in, machine list, pairing).
- Requests that fail before the telemetry door is initialized are not reported.
- Errors a query function throws after a successful HTTP response (parse or shape checks) are not reported as client_request_failed.
- No change to packages/anywhere-channel.
- No route vocabulary beyond ROUTE_SCOPES for desktop admin routes; they report route=other with a route_area.
- No raw path, URL, response body, conversation name or id, machine label or environment id in any event.
- No changes in eltmon/overdeck-landing, App Store Connect or Play Console, and no TestFlight upload by the work agent; these are post-merge operator steps recorded in apps/mobile/acceptance/PAN-5100.md.

autoDecisions.summary: Capture request failures with a single fetch wrapper instead of QueryCache/MutationCache onError handlers.
autoDecisions.rationale: The cache handlers receive only the Error each query function builds (e.g. 'Failed to load conversations: 500'), so route and status are unavailable there; 236 frontend files call fetch directly. The fetch layer sees URL, method and status for every request, as apps/mobile/src/shell/requestLog.ts already does.
A fetch wrapper cannot know which query called it; route already names the failing endpoint.

autoDecisions.summary: route is a closed domain built from ROUTE_SCOPES paths plus 'other', with a separate closed route_area from the no-loss matrix.
autoDecisions.rationale: tests/unit/contracts/telemetry-schema.test.ts forbids broad string property values; ROUTE_SCOPES is exactly the phone-callable surface, and route_area keeps desktop admin failures diagnosable without any id ever being sent.

autoDecisions.summary: client, platform, app_version, build_commit, install_kind and install_id are PostHog super properties, not catalog properties (client is also in the client_request_failed catalog).
autoDecisions.rationale: app_version and build_commit are free strings the closed catalog cannot hold; super properties also put client=phone on $exception events, as the issue requires.

autoDecisions.summary: PAN-5100's decisions (machine setting, machine install id) override PAN-5021's (phone switch, separate id); keep PAN-5021's in-memory persistence.
autoDecisions.rationale: PAN-5100 is the newer, explicit operator decision for this scope; in-memory persistence stops one machine's id leaking into another machine's events because opening a machine reloads the page.

autoDecisions.summary: The phone caches the last client-config answer per machine and initializes from a cached 'on' immediately.
autoDecisions.rationale: Without it a link that is down from the start (the reported 'Couldn't load conversations' case) could never be reported, because consent comes from the machine. A fresh 'off' disables capture and clears the cache; sign-out clears all caches.

autoDecisions.summary: The machine returns the PostHog key and host in the client config; when telemetry is off it returns only effectiveEnabled:false.
autoDecisions.rationale: The phone's Vite root does not load the frontend's .env.production; the machine already owns these values in AnalyticsService, and nothing identifying leaves the machine when telemetry is off.

autoDecisions.summary: phone_link_state uses a new link_reason domain that reuses link_failure_reason spellings where meanings match.
autoDecisions.rationale: linkFailureReason maps MachineLinkError codes the phone never throws, and link_failure_reason lacks none/removed/drop reasons; sharing spellings keeps PostHog breakdowns comparable.

autoDecisions.summary: A link drop is the /ws/rpc connection phase leaving 'live' after it was live once; a drop within 5 s of a foreground resume has reason 'resume'.
autoDecisions.rationale: MachineDialer exposes only onRecovered; the phase is the operator-visible symptom and needs no change to packages/anywhere-channel.

autoDecisions.summary: app_version is APP_VERSION from apps/mobile/src/shell/config.ts, not version.ts.
autoDecisions.rationale: version.ts only compares versions; config.ts line 10 reads apps/mobile/package.json.

autoDecisions.summary: Update the phone's store privacy declarations in this PR.
autoDecisions.rationale: privacy-app.html, RELEASE.md and PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy state the app has no analytics or crash reporting; shipping posthog-js with them unchanged is a false declaration.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep the phone link-state reporter in this issue rather than a sibling issue, with a sizeJustification.
autoDecisions.rationale: Phone builds are uploaded by hand; one TestFlight build and one privacy review should cover all phone diagnostics.

autoDecisions.summary: Report phone 403s on admin routes as client_request_failed like any other failure.
autoDecisions.rationale: They are the phone UI's remaining scope gaps (PAN-4835 H-4), which is diagnostic; the scope inventory apps/mobile/request-log.json holds one such row and the 60 s throttle bounds repeats.

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-4b: track loaded vs initialized; disableTelemetry() calls posthog.opt_out_capturing() when loaded, sets initialized false and clears pending exceptions; an 'on' config when already loaded calls posthog.opt_in_capturing({ captureEventName: false }) and re-registers super properties instead of a second posthog.init; a first init with an 'on' config also opts in when posthog.has_opted_out_capturing() returns true. captureException before init queues up to PENDING_EXCEPTION_LIMIT = 5 entries, flushed once on an 'on' init and discarded on an 'off' init or disable. capture() and captureException() wrap posthog calls in try/catch.

items.title: Given on → disableTelemetry() → on, the door calls opt_out_capturing then opt_in_capturing({ captureEventName: false }), posthog.init receives exactly one call, and a later capture() reaches posthog.capture
Given has_opted_out_capturing() returns true at first init and the config is on, the door calls opt_in_capturing({ captureEventName: false })
Given a captureException before init, an 'on' init sends exactly one posthog.captureException and an 'off' init sends none; seven pre-init exceptions produce at most five sends
Given posthog.capture and posthog.captureException throw, capture() and captureException() return without throwing

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-5: new lib/requestFailures.ts with installRequestFailureObserver({ client, target?, report?, now? }) and classifyFetchRejection(); same-origin /api/ and /events/ paths only (pathOf copied from apps/mobile/src/shell/requestLog.ts); route and route_area only from clientRouteOf; status via bucketRequestStatus or the rejection class; method bucketed to the http_method domain; throttle key route+area+status for 60 s; report wrapped in try/catch; return the inner response unchanged and rethrow the same rejection. Call installRequestFailureObserver({ client: 'desktop' }) in main.tsx on the line before void initTelemetry(). Add the test file to scripts/frontend-test-subset.txt in sorted position. Use fake timers for the throttle test and construct DOMException TimeoutError/AbortError directly.

items.title: Given a 500 on GET /api/conversations, the observer reports exactly { client: 'desktop', route: '/api/conversations', route_area: 'conversations', method: 'GET', status: '500' } once, and the caller receives the original response object
Given a second identical failure within 60 s, the observer sends no report; after advancing fake timers by 60 000 ms the next failure emits a report again
A rejected fetch reports network for TypeError, timeout for DOMException TimeoutError, aborted for DOMException AbortError, and rethrows the same error object
Given a 2xx response, a cross-host URL (https://us.i.posthog.com/e/) or a throwing report function, the observer emits no report and returns the inner response unchanged
A failure on /api/projects/secret-key/thing emits a payload in which no value contains the string 'secret-key'

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-9b: export lastResumedAt() from lifecycle.ts; new linkTelemetry.ts with installLinkTelemetry(deps) and linkReasonOf() using the PRD's mapping and the four behaviors (failed throttled per reason for 60 s; dropped only after the phase was live once, reason 'resume' within 5 000 ms of a resume else the phase name; recovered with bucketRecoveryMs; route_changed only when a previous route for the same id differs). In ShellApp's services effect create the reporter before createConnection, pass onLinkOpened, subscribe to useConnectionState with deriveConnectionPhase, and uninstall in the cleanup. Fake timers in tests. The reporter takes currentEnvironmentId (currentMachineId from ./store) and routeOpened ignores any other machine before touching state, because notification-preference sync opens links to every paired machine over the same connection.
